Article Title: ‘Silence any woman who dares to ask questions’: Rahul slams Delhi Police over sexual harassment complaints
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi sl. ams Delhi Police over women journalists' complaints

What Delhi Police said about the protest

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Monday accused the Delhi Police of mistreating women protesters and journalists during recent demonstrations in the national capital, after three women who identified themselves as journalists complained of alleged manhandling and sexual harassment by police personnel.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi alleged that women were being silenced when they raised questions and demanded that CCTV footage from Saket police station be made public. He also sought action against police personnel accused of misconduct."What’s happening in Delhi right now follows a single pattern: silence any woman who dares to ask questions.Hundreds of people were detained at Jantar Mantar. Female protesters alleged that male police officers misbehaved with them. Cameras were snatched from female journalists, and they were dragged around. Not even an FIR was filed on a journalist’s complaint.A few weeks ago, Shaheen and Nafisa recounted their experiences of violence and mistreatment inside the Saket police station. Think about it—inside the station, the very place where women go to file complaints.Those entrusted with the responsibility of protecting women are now the ones posing a threat to them.And everyone in this country knows who the Delhi Police answers to.The entire CCTV footage from the Saket police station should be made public. Immediate action must be taken against the guilty police officers. Shaheen, Nafisa, and all those who have faced violence and rudeness from the Delhi Police must get justice.Mr Amit Shah—why are you and your police so afraid of women?"The Delhi Police, meanwhile, said three women journalists had submitted complaints alleging that they were manhandled by police officers and staff during their detention at a protest on October 3 against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Deputy commissioner of police Neha Yadav said the complaints had been registered, medical examinations conducted and the matter referred to the Crime Branch.“Around 6 PM, three women, who identified themselves as journalists, lodged a complaint alleging manhandling by Delhi Police officers and staff during their detention."“We request anyone possessing relevant footage to share it with the Crime Branch,” Yadav said.Delhi Police also confirmed that it had received complaints alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during the October 3 protest.“On 03-10-26, during the protest in New Delhi area, while being in law and order situation, allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers. New Delhi District has received their complaints,” the police said in a post on X.According to police, protesters had been asked to vacate the site after Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita was imposed in the area. The protesters allegedly refused to comply and were subsequently detained.“Despite the imposition of Section 163 of the BNSS in the area, AISA and other parties staged a protest on October 3rd against the SIR. Protesters were warned to vacate the site, citing Section 163 of the BNSS; upon their refusal to comply, they were detained,” Yadav said.Several members of the All India Students' Association were detained by Delhi Police during the protest near Jantar Mantar. The demonstration was held against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as protests over the SIR exercise continued in the capital.Several protesters, including AISA president Neha Bora and senior advocates Prashant Bhushan and Kapil Sibal, attempted to cross police barricades near Jantar Mantar, according to the police account.Delhi Police has registered at least three FIRs in connection with the mass protest held near Jantar Mantar on October 2. Two FIRs were registered at Parliament Street police station and one at Connaught Place police station.
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi accuses delhi police of mistreating women protesters and journalists. Three women who identified themselves as journalists complained of alleged manhandling and sexual harassment by police personnel. Delhi police said three women journalists had submitted complaints alleging they were manhandled by police officers and staff during their detention.

Article Title: Ex-TMC MP Koel Mallick joins BJP a day after being nominated for Rajya Sabha seat
Article Text:
Bengali film actor Koyel Mallick joins BJP.

NEW DELHI: Bengali film actor Koel Mallick joined the BJP on Monday, a day after the party nominated her for the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections.Mallick, daughter of veteran Bengali actor Ranjit Mallick, had earlier served as a TMC Rajya Sabha MP for a brief period from April 6 to July 16. She resigned after the Mamata Banerjee-led party's electoral setback in the assembly elections.West Bengal BJP general secretary Sashi Agnihotri welcomed Mallick into the party and said she would file her nomination for the Rajya Sabha seat on Monday.“It would be an honour for me to become a member of the Upper House of Parliament and get a chance to work for the welfare of the people,” Mallick said at a press conference at the BJP state headquarters.The actor said she wanted to be part of the development initiatives undertaken by the BJP government in West Bengal. She also thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari for selecting her for the Rajya Sabha nomination.Asked about criticism over her decision to leave the TMC and join the BJP, Mallick said, “They are making such rude comments possibly because of their own vexations. I have no anger against them,” PTI reported.She said the new government was taking steps to create opportunities for Bengal's talent and prevent people from leaving the state, adding that she wanted to contribute to those efforts.“The root cause of increasing toxicity on social media is lack of work among the people,” she added.Responding to a question on whether joining the TMC had been a wrong decision, Mallick said, “Every party has its own ways of working and doing good. I feel enormously proud and privileged that I am now in a party which has undertaken welfare works for people in West Bengal in the past few months.”The bypolls for 12 Rajya Sabha seats across West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand are scheduled for October 16.
Article Summary: Bengali film actor koyel mallick joins bjp. Mallick had earlier served as a tmc rajya sabha mp for a brief period. She resigned after the mamata banerjee-led party's electoral setback in the assembly elections.

NEW DELHI : Delhi Police on Monday detained protesters outside Parliament Street Police Station who were demonstrating against an alleged incident of sexual misconduct against three women journalists during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar.The protesters were detained following a clash with police officers. One of the protesters stated that they had been demonstrating against the incident from 6:00 PM yesterday until 6:00 AM. The Police detained them at 7:00 in the morning.The protester further alleged that despite merely demanding the registration of an FIR, police personnel treated them poorly and took them into custody."We've been here since last night. We've been sitting here from 6:00 PM yesterday until 6:00 AM today, and it's almost 7:00 now. All we're asking is for an FIR to be filed. Instead, the police are treating us terribly, detaining us, and She's the victim of a sexual assault, and they beat her up too after dragging her away. All she wants is for an FIR to be filed," said protestors.Another protester alleged that police personnel have been using sticks inside to assault demonstrators, claiming that women and disabled persons were also beaten by police officials."They are beating the disabled person, they are beating the woman, a stick is being used inside," said another protester.Explaining the reason for their presence, one protester said that they had gathered at the spot to inquire about the status of the complaint regarding the October 3 assault incident."The police are misbehaving with us... We are here to ask for the status of our complaint after 48 hours..." said Protestors.Earlier, three women journalists alleged sexual harassment by police personnel during a protest at Jantar Mantar on October 3.Following the incident, Delhi Police received their complaints and transferred the matter to the Crime Branch, Kamla Market."On 03-10-26, during the protest in New Delhi area, while being in law and order situation, allegations of sexual harassment were made by three female journalists against police officers. Article Title: 'Ensure women safety, even at 10pm': SC tells Delhi authorities to be 'very harsh' in rape crackdown

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday stressed the need for stronger measures to prevent crimes against women in Delhi, saying authorities must create an environment where women feel safe while walking on the streets or travelling by public transport.A bench led by Justice JB Pardiwala was hearing a suo motu case initiated by the court over recent rape cases and other crimes against women in Delhi-NCR."There appears to be a feeling that women are not safe in city particularly in some vulnerable pockets," the court observed, flagging concerns over the safety of women in certain parts of the national capital.The bench told the Centre and Delhi Police that the focus should be on preventing crimes rather than dealing with them after they have occurred."We must ensure every woman in NCT Delhi feels safe, whether walking at 10 PM or travelling by metro or road," the court said.The Supreme Court also said deficiencies in the system should not create conditions that allow crimes to take place."Deficiencies, if any, should not facilitate commission of crime," the court said."What is important is to prevent crime, not what you do after crime is committed," it observed.The court also stressed the need to create a strong deterrent for those who may be inclined to commit such offences.“Unless you don’t create such fright in the minds if the criminals ki ab kuch kiya toh mar jayengey (if we commit such a crime we will die) you will not be able to prevent such crimes”, Justice JB Pardiwala said.“You need to create a fright, a fear in the mind of a man who is prone to commit such officers”, the judge said.The Supreme Court told Delhi Police that it should take a firm approach against those accused of committing serious crimes against women, while also referring to concerns that could be raised under Article 21, which guarantees the right to life and personal liberty.The court said authorities should not be deterred from taking strict action against those accused of rape and other serious offences because of criticism from human rights groups.
Article Summary: Sc raps centre, delhi police over recent rape incidents and other crimes against women. "there appears to be a feeling that women are not safe in city particularly in some vulnerable pockets," the court observed. The court also stressed the need to create a strong deterrent for those who may be inclined to commit such offences.

Article Title: Second Vande Bharat sleeper set to launch this month between Bengaluru and Mumbai; cutting travel time from 24 hours to under 16 hours, 30 year wait for faster connectivity between two cities to end
Article Text:
For more than 30 years, passengers have been seeking faster rail connectivity between Bengaluru and Mumbai.

Mumbai-Bengaluru Vande Bharat Sleeper: Expected Travel Time

What makes Vande Bharat sleeper special?

Vande Bharat sleeper: Indian Railways is all set to roll out the second Vande Bharat sleeper train after launching the first pair between Guwahati and Howrah earlier this year.After prolonged delays, the Railway Board is expected to issue the notification for the KSR Bengaluru-Mumbai CSMT Vande Bharat Sleeper shortly. According to sources, the train is likely to be flagged off later this month.The country's second Vande Bharat sleeper service is expected to substantially reduce the time taken to travel by rail between Bengaluru, India's technology hub, and Mumbai, its financial capital.Also Read | With better than Rajdhani experience & 160 kmph speed, can Vande Bharat sleeper trains be a game-changer for Indian Railways? Under the proposed schedule, the premium train will run six days a week in each direction, covering the distance in under 16 hours. At present, the Udyan Express, the only direct daily train connecting the two cities, takes an average of 24 hours to complete the journey.As per the tentative timings, the service may leave KSR Bengaluru at 10 PM and arrive at Mumbai CSMT at 1:50 PM the next day. On the return journey, it could start from Mumbai at 10:30 PM, reaching Bengaluru at 1:50 PM the following day. These are tentative timings and are subject to change.Although the official launch date has not yet been declared, the railway zones have been asked to commence the service at the earliest convenient opportunity.Its scheduled halts will include Anantapur, Guntakal, Raichur, Kalaburagi, Solapur and Kalyan, according to this TOI report For more than 30 years, passengers have been seeking faster rail connectivity between Bengaluru and Mumbai. Despite repeated assurances, train journeys between the two cities continue to take considerable time.The proposed Vande Bharat Sleeper service is expected to address this long-standing demand and improve connectivity between the cities.The Vande Bharat sleeper train has 16 passenger coaches. The rake includes 11 AC 3-tier coaches, four AC 2-tier coaches and one AC First Class coach.The train has been designed to operate at speeds of up to 160 kmph, while its testing speed is 180 kmph, placing it in the semi-high-speed category. However, most sections of the Indian Railways network are not equipped to permit trains to operate at such high speeds.Drawing on design elements seen in European trains, the Vande Bharat sleeper coaches feature cushioned berths aimed at providing greater comfort. The design of the upper berths has also been modified to make climbing up easier for passengers.Passenger amenities include dedicated night lights, integrated public announcement systems accompanied by visual displays, CCTV cameras and modular pantry units.The sleeper train is also equipped with modern bio-vacuum toilets similar to those used in aircraft. A separate toilet designed for disabled passengers also has a baby care station. Passengers travelling in AC First Class additionally have access to shower facilities with hot water.For safety, the Vande Bharat sleeper train comes fitted with the indigenous KAVACH anti-collision system. Like the chair car versions of Vande Bharat, the sleeper variant will also use regenerative braking technology to improve energy efficiency.Automatic interconnecting doors have been provided between the coaches. The gangways are fully sealed, helping maintain clean air inside the train as well as effective temperature control.Passenger convenience features in every coach include individual reading lights, charging points and refreshment tables. The interiors use GFRP panels. The train doors are designed to open automatically at designated stations.The train also comes with a Centralised Coach Monitoring System. An emergency communication facility allows passengers to communicate directly with the driver when required.Meanwhile, ICF is also working on developing its own version of the Vande Bharat sleeper train.
Article Summary: The ksr bengaluru-mumbai csmt vande bharat sleeper is likely to be flagged off later this month. The premium train will run six days a week in each direction, covering the distance in under 16 hours. At present, the udyan express, the only direct daily train connecting the two cities, takes an average of 24 hours.

Article Title: 'Want to see who modified Form 6': SC refuses to pass interim order to suspend CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Article Text:
SC on Monday heard two pleas against CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

What did the petitioners seek?

What is the EC SIR row?

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday refused to pass an interim order seeking the suspension of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and issued notice to the Election Commission of India, CEC and the other two election commissioners on a plea challenging decisions taken by the poll body on Special Intensive Revision.A bench led by CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard pleas filed by Patna resident Rakesh Kumar Singh and advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi. The pleas raised questions over whether Gyanesh used powers belonging to the Election Commission without the approval of election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.“Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear. When record has produced, we would like to see who has modified. But, your prayers appear jumbled up,” the CJI noted, as quoted by LiveLaw.The apex court directed the respondents to file their responses to the allegations. The court said it would examine whether the statutory scheme was followed and indicated that if the records showed that any decision was not taken in accordance with the law, it could injunct such a decision and hold it ultra vires"If records show some decision was not unanimous etc., we will injunct those decisions and say they are ultra-vires.Can we ex-parte come to decision that all decisions were unilateral? We expect them to respond in a clear, transparent manner," Justice Bagchi added.One of the plea sought Gyanesh's suspension until the final hearing to protect the “multi-member character of the Election Commission”. It asked that Sandhu and Joshi run the commission's business together in the meantime and that any vacancy be filled on the recommendation of a committee that includes the Chief Justice of India.However, the second plea sought criminal proceedings against the CEC and other officials for allegedly failing in their official duty. It further sought a declaration that all decisions, guidelines and software changes made under Gyanesh without the full commission's agreement are “unconstitutional, ultra vires and void ab initio”, meaning illegal and invalid from the start.Tripathi's plea relies on Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, which says the majority view prevails when commissioners differ. The plea argued that the law requires decisions to be taken together.A report by the Indian Express claimed that commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders relating to the SIR, which were allegedly issued without their knowledge or recommendation.On Form 6, the voter registration form, the plea alleges that a requirement for ancestral details and a link to the previous SIR was added through the poll panel's software without the legal amendment the election rules require. It claims the other two commissioners objected to the change.On Goa, it alleges that the software lacked a feature to restore 97 eligible voters despite directions to verify them.On West Bengal, it claims more than 16.10 lakh appeals were filed in the EC's name against voters whose names were restored by judicial officers. It says the other two commissioners and the state's chief electoral officer did not know about these appeals or approve them.The Election Commission has said differing views are a normal part of discussions in any institution and that all its orders are legally valid and follow the set procedures.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at okhla that existed before january 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

What the evidence points to

Animals do not simply move on when their habitat shrinks. Their numbers thin out

Over the past fifty years, the average size of monitored wildlife populations around the world has fallen by 73 per cent, according to WWF's Living Planet Report 2024. The report names loss and degradation of habitat as the most commonly reported threat, driven mainly by how the world grows its food.This finding raises a plain question. When animals lose the land, water and forest they depend on, what happens to them?Habitat rarely disappears all at once. It is cut into pieces by farms, roads, canals, railway lines, power lines and growing towns. Each piece may still have trees and water, but it supports fewer animals than the original whole did.The 73 per cent figure also needs careful reading. It describes the average change across thousands of monitored populations. It does not mean that three-quarters of the world's animals are gone, or that three-quarters of species have disappeared. What it does show is a steady thinning, and the report describes such declines as an early warning of greater risk to species and ecosystems. The pressure it describes is gradual and widespread rather than the result of a single event, which is partly why it is easy to overlook. The report also notes that some populations have held steady or recovered where conservation has worked.“This is not just about wildlife, it’s about the essential ecosystems that sustain human life,” said Daudi Sumba, chief conservation officer at WWF.The effects usually arrive in a recognisable order. Food and water become harder to find, so animals travel farther to reach them. Their routes cross fields, highways and railway tracks. Animals with large ranges, such as elephants and big cats, are affected first, because they need the most room.Smaller populations face a slower problem. When forest patches are cut off from one another, animals cannot move between them to find mates. Over time a small, isolated group becomes more vulnerable to disease and to sudden shocks such as drought or fire. Wherever forest meets farmland or settlement, animals and people also meet more often, and not always safely.India's elephants show how this plays out. The country holds about 60 per cent of the world's Asian elephants, according to the last census in 2017. Most of them do not live inside protected areas. Government and press figures put the share outside reserves at about 80 per cent. That share matters for everything that follows. A herd that lives mostly outside reserves has no boundary between it and the land that people farm, travel across and build on.For these herds, a journey between feeding grounds can pass through paddy fields, village lanes, rail lines and overhead power cables. Official data tabled in Parliament in 2024 shows what that means. Over five years, the leading cause of unnatural elephant deaths was electrocution, ahead of train accidents, poaching and poisoning. Odisha, Assam, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu reported the largest numbers of electrocution deaths.The government has taken some steps in response. It has identified and ground-validated about 150 elephant corridors, the routes herds use to move between forests. The Railways and Environment ministries have also formed a standing committee to reduce deaths on tracks.Tigers tell a more hopeful story, with a warning attached. The 2022 estimate counted at least 3,682 tigers in India, a record, spread across 53 tiger reserves. These reserves are among the best protected forests in the country.But the same assessment shows the limits of protection. Roughly a third of the reserves need stronger protection, habitat restoration or more prey for the tigers to feed on. A few reserves in Mizoram, Nagaland and Jharkhand reported almost no tigers at all. Summaries of the report also describe many reserves as small islands of forest, joined to one another by a limited number of corridors. A reserve with a healthy tiger population can send young animals out in search of territory of their own, and many of them end up in unprotected land among farms and villages.The record count and the weak reserves belong in the same account. Protection works where it is applied well, and the gaps appear where it is not.Kaziranga's protection does not stop at the park boundary, and a new proposal from the Assam government has put that line under debate. The state wants to replace the default 10-km eco-sensitive zone (ESZ) around Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve with a site-specific zone of one to three kilometres. An ESZ is a regulatory buffer, declared by the environment ministry on a state's proposal. It is not an outright ban: depending on the notification, activities in it may be prohibited, regulated or permitted, and mining is among those most strictly restricted.Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma says the 10-km limit applies only because Kaziranga has not yet been finally notified. He argues it brings populated areas such as Kaliabor, Doboka and Jakhalabandha under restrictions, and holds up civic projects like a proposed stadium in Bokakhat. The state says the park's boundary and its UNESCO World Heritage status will not change, and that the 10-km zone stays in force until a new one is notified. Some residents agree. Hundreds rallied in support of the proposal on August 18, saying the current limits get in the way of building homes and basic infrastructure.The opposition and conservationists are not convinced. Congress state president Gaurav Gogoi led a protest at the Kohora range and alleged that the change could give legal cover to mining. The state government rejects the charge. Conservationists such as Jadav Payeng and Kavita Ashok point to the annual floods, when rhinos, deer and elephants move to higher ground outside the park. A smaller zone, they warn, could cut off those routes.A 2025 conservation assessment notes that a smaller zone is not necessarily a weaker one if it is designed to protect the most sensitive areas. Whether it does will depend on the final notification, which will decide whether wildlife corridors, flood escape routes and wetlands fall inside the line.Space does not only mean forest. Globally, freshwater species have seen the steepest declines in the WWF report, and wetlands are often among the first places to be drained or built over.The report points to Chennai, where rapid urban growth has led to a large loss of wetland area. Wetlands shelter birds, fish and amphibians, and they also soak up floodwater for the city around them. When they go, wildlife loses a home and people lose a buffer.When space runs out, people pay too. Government data tabled in Parliament showed that elephants killed 2,853 people in India over five years, with the highest toll in 2023. Many of these deaths happened in places where farms, villages and elephant routes overlap. The elephant deaths and the human deaths come from the same stretches of land, where both now depend on the same ground.The Environment Ministry has issued guidelines on managing human-elephant conflict, and it says compensation is provided for losses. These measures respond to the damage after it happens. They do not by themselves restore the space that animals have lost.Some efforts aim at the cause. West Bengal has begun a community programme called Gajamitra, or Friends of Elephants, in which local people take part in reducing conflict. Conservation scientists have also suggested low-cost methods for farmers, such as planting chillies, ginger or citrus around fields, which elephants tend to avoid, or placing beehives along field edges.The WWF report also records progress in India, where it says some wildlife populations have stabilised or recovered. It credits government initiatives, careful habitat management, scientific monitoring and community involvement. At the global level, the report calls for more effective conservation along with changes in food, energy and finance systems.The picture from India and from the world is consistent. Animals do not simply move on when their habitat shrinks. Their numbers thin out, they wander into danger, they come into conflict with people, or they disappear from places they once held. Where land is protected, connected and shared with the people who live beside it, some populations hold their ground or recover.India's own examples point in both directions: electrocutions and train deaths on one side, a record tiger count and recovering populations on the other. The difference lies largely in whether land is protected and linked together, and whether the people who live beside wildlife are part of the plan.The question on World Wildlife Day is how much room is left for wildlife, and who decides what happens to it.
Article Summary: India holds about 60 per cent of the world's asian elephants. The average size of monitored wildlife populations around the world has fallen by 73 per cent. Loss and degradation of habitat is the most commonly reported threat. A third of the reserves need stronger protection, habitat restoration or more prey for the tigers to feed on.

Article Title: 'I do not accept': Ex-Maha CM Chavan rejects Raj Thackeray’s election boycott call amid SIR row
Article Text:
Ex-Maha CM Chavan challenges Raj Thackeray’s Maharashtra strategy

Former Maharashtra chief minister and senior Congress leader Prithviraj Chavan on Sunday rejected Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) chief Raj Thackeray ’s call to boycott elections, saying participation in elections was a democratic right.“I do not accept that we should boycott the election. It is our right to a democratic government; that is not a correct strategy,” Chavan said.Chavan made the remarks amid a political confrontation over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Maharashtra and the functioning of the Election Commission. On Sunday, Raj Thackeray and Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray led a joint protest march in Mumbai against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, demanding the cancellation of the SIR exercise and raising questions over the poll panel’s functioning.Recalling the 2024 election, Chavan said he had raised concerns over alleged duplicate voters being added to electoral rolls and voting multiple times.“When my election took place in 2024, I protested, saying in my case duplicate voters were added who voted multiple times,” he said.Chavan further alleged that some minority and poor voters had been denied their voting rights, including people who supported the Congress.“In some places, minority voters were deprived of voting rights; in some places, poor people were deprived of voting rights; those who favoured the Congress party,” he said.“This is not vote chori; it is election chori,” Chavan alleged.His remarks came as the Thackeray cousins jointly led what was described as the ‘Virat Garjana Morcha’ in Mumbai, with Congress and NCP (SP) leaders also participating. Raj Thackeray called for the SIR exercise in Maharashtra to be scrapped and for elections to return to ballot papers.“Our demand is that the entire SIR conducted in Maharashtra should be cancelled,” Raj Thackeray said.“The law says that SIR is conducted if an emergency situation arises,” he said, questioning the circumstances in which the revision was undertaken.Raj Thackeray also alleged that 40 to 60 lakh voters were added during the Maharashtra Assembly elections and claimed that two crore voters were now being removed through SIR.“Forty to sixty lakh voters were added during the Assembly elections, and power was captured through this. And now, through SIR, two crore people are being removed. Who are these two crore voters?” he asked.Uddhav Thackeray separately questioned the appointment process for Election Commissioners and criticised the removal of the Chief Justice of India from the selection committee.“The first question is how was Gyanesh Kumar appointed?” Thackeray asked.The Election Commission has maintained that the electoral-roll revision is intended to update and clean the rolls, with mechanisms available for claims and objections.
Article Summary: Ex-maha cm chavan challenges raj thackeray’s maharashtra strategy. Chavan: ‘i do not accept that we should boycott the election. It is our right to a democratic government; that is not a correct strategy’ raj and uddhav led a joint protest march against chief election commissioner gyanesh kumar.

HC rejected pleas seeking registration of FIRs.

NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Monday dismissed a batch of petitions seeking an SIT probe into the 2020 Delhi riotsand the violence at Jamia Millia Islamia during anti-CAA protests in December 2019.A bench of Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Manoj Jain said, “for the reasons mentioned in the judgment, all the petitions are dismissed”.“The batch is decided into two parts, one is northeast Delhi riots and another is for Jamia Millia riots,” the bench said while pronouncing the verdict, PTI reported.The court also rejected pleas seeking registration of FIRs against political leaders over alleged “hate speeches” linked to the 2020 riots and action against police officers accused of dereliction of duty. The court had reserved its verdict on the petitions on July 24.In the northeast Delhi riots matter, the petitions sought directions for setting up an SIT, a commission of inquiry or a fact-finding committee to examine various aspects of the violence.The pleas also sought medical treatment and compensation for those affected, besides registration of FIRs against police officers accused of lapses. Some petitioners also sought FIRs against political leaders over alleged hate speeches.A communal clash broke out in northeast Delhi on February 24, 2020, amid protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act. At least 53 people were killed and around 700 injured in the violence.Shaikh Mujtaba sought FIRs against BJP leaders Kapil Mishra, Anurag Thakur, Parvesh Verma and Abhay Verma over their speeches.Lawyers Voice sought FIRs over alleged hate speeches by several leaders, including Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Manish Sisodia, Amanatullah Khan, Akbaruddin Owaisi and Waris Pathan.CPI(M) leader Brinda Karat sought an independent probe into alleged excesses by police, Rapid Action Force personnel and other officials.Another petitioner, Ajay Gautam, sought an NIA probe into the alleged funding of anti-CAA protests, along with FIRs against political leaders over alleged inflammatory speeches, ANI reported.The Supreme Court had earlier asked the high court to decide one of the pleas expeditiously. The other petitions concerned violence at Jamia Millia Islamia during anti-CAA protests in December 2019.Students alleged that police assaulted them during the protests and sought an independent probe into the alleged police action. In some petitions, the petitioners also sought transfer of the investigation from the Delhi Police to an outside agency.One petitioner, Nabila Hasan, who was then a law student, had also approached the National Human Rights Commission.The Delhi Police opposed the pleas, saying it had collected and preserved CCTV footage from cameras inside and outside the university and in the New Friends Colony area. It also argued that transferring the investigation would unnecessarily widen the scope of the proceedings.
Article Summary: Hc rejected pleas seeking registration of firs. At least 53 people were killed and around 700 injured in the violence. The delhi police opposed the pleas, saying it had collected and preserved cctv footage from cameras inside and outside the university and in the new friends colony area.

Article Title: Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman
Article Text:
I hope SC steps in and rectifies these things, Justice Nariman said

NEW DELHI: Ahead of a Supreme Court hearing Monday on the SIR controversy and a plea seeking suspension of the CEC for his "unilateral decisions", former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman Sunday flagged "malfunctioning" of the poll panel and said a citizen's right to vote, which is at the heart of democracy, was in great peril because of "illegal knocking out" of people from voters' lists.Justice Nariman also highlighted the problem in the appointment process of election commissioners, which is in Centre's hands. He expressed hope SC would rise to the occasion and rectify the mistakes prevailing in the system.He said around 93% of adjudicated cases of deleted voters in West Bengal had been decided in their favour which meant they were illegally removed. TOI had first reported on September 20 that appellate tribunals had upheld deletion of only 8,649 voters out of the 1.2 lakh cases decided so far.Also read: Lawyers’ body forms panel to review SIR: Ex-SC, HC judges to examine ‘constitutional & statutory validity’ "Now, the unfortunate part is that all this came before the court very recently. Two judges differed, and the ultimate thing is now it has gone before a bench, probably of five judges, in order to find out whether this is good law or not... But meanwhile, these appointments continue only in the hands of govt of the day. Now, we saw the danger of this happening very recently. All of you have seen that in the Bengal elections, 90 lakh voters were disenfranchised.That is an astounding figure. Ninety lakh voters getting disenfranchised did not somehow move Supreme Court enough to stay this," Justice Nariman said.Out of those who were disenfranchised, around 22 lakh filed appeals, the former SC judge said, adding, "The others must be people who don't have the wherewithal or access to justice."Justice Nariman pointed out that of 1 lakh appeals, almost all were decided in favour of the voters. "So, you can imagine this was completely illegal - knocking out of the common man, the citizen of India in order that a govt obtains what it wants. And in Bengal, we saw it ousted govt of the day and brought in govt of Centre. Now, these are very, very disturbing things that are happening in our country today," he said, speaking on 'The Constitution and the Common Man' at Rajkumar College, Rajkot."I hope the apex court, the institution to which I once belonged, steps in immediately and rectifies these things. You can't have an EC which functions or malfunctions like this. So the first important red flag qua the Constitution and the common man is the appointment process of election commissioners. The sooner the constitution bench decides you have to have somebody like a PM, leader of the opposition coupled with the Chief Justice or his nominee, who then picks the best names in order to see that votes actually translate into what they were supposed to translate into happens," Justice Nariman said.
Article Summary: Former sc judge justice rohinton fali nariman sunday flagged "malfunctioning" of the poll panel. He said a citizen's right to vote was in great peril because of "illegal knocking out" of people from voters' lists. He expressed hope sc would rise to the occasion and rectify the mistakes prevailing in the system.

Article Title: 'Look Out Circular' against parents of man who secretly took away child to US
Article Text:
SC said that all attempts were being made by the man’s parents to surreptitiously leave the country and obstruct the course of justice

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: It is increasingly becoming common in matrimonial disputes involving NRI couples, particularly child custody cases, for one spouse to take the child to a foreign country where he or she works and refuse to submit to the jurisdiction of Indian courts, leaving the other partner behind. Now, Supreme Court has indicated that in such cases, the parents of the runaway partner have to face the consequences.Hearing such a case, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan revived a 'Look Out Circular' - monitor, trace, or restrict travel of individuals - against the parents of a man who clandestinely took away his three-and-a-half-year-old daughter to the US, without informing his wife, and has refused to bring her back to India."The minor child, at the relevant point of time, aged three-and-a-half years, was taken away by the father to US. The mother is relentlessly trying to get her daughter back. The mother is in a pathetic condition. We have no idea in what circumstances the minor daughter is residing in US with her father, that too a working father," the bench said.It added that all attempts are being made by the man's parents to surreptitiously leave this country and obstruct the course of justice."We have stayed the operation of the order passed by Madras High Court setting aside the Look Out Circular," the bench said.It granted the man a last chance to come back to India with the minor child. "We have made ourselves more than clear that he has to come to India within four weeks from the US with her, failing which his parents will have to face severe legal consequences. We have made the parents understand in vernacular," Supreme Court said.The bench said that if he was not inclined to come to India within four weeks, then he should make necessary arrangements to put the child on board along with an escort. It also asked him to hand over the child to the mother if she reached US."We have passed this order keeping in mind the interest of the child, who was taken-away by her father deceitfully when she was just three-and-a-half years of age. Why should she be deprived of the love, care and affection of her own mother? Why should he stay back in US along with the daughter?" the court said in its order and posted the hearing after a month.
Article Summary: Sc said that all attempts were being made by the man’s parents to surreptitiously leave the country and obstruct the course of justice. The mother is relentlessly trying to get her daughter back. We have no idea in what circumstances the minor daughter is residing in us with her father, that too a working father.
